text.p: Computer training company Informatics Holdings Ltd is looking at expanding into Europe, group managing director Ong Boon Kheng said on Tuesday.
Speaking to reporters to review the group's 1997 results, Ong said Informatics' recent move to acquire NCC Services Ltd (NCC) in the United Kingdom was a step in that direction.
Informatics paid 2.15 million sterling pounds to buy the education division of U.K. based National Computing Centre in April.
"NCC is a good platform for Informatics to launch into Europe...We will be using NCC to launch the Informatics franchise into Europe," Ong said.

Ong said it was too early to say when Informatics will start its first training centre in Europe, as the company was still exploring ways to see how it could leverage on NCC's strength of having an established accreditation programme with the Informatics franchise.
Ong said there were some ongoing negotiations with interested parties in Eastern Europe but nothing has been finalised.
On current year prospects, Ong said the group expects to maintain the earnings growth momentum achieved in recent years.
"We have 20 to 25 percent growth in the last few years. Looking at the trend, we expect growth to be sustained," he said.
Informatics reported a 20.4 percent rise in after tax profit to Singapore $8.28 million for the year ended March 31, 1997.
Ong said the bulk of the group's earnings or about 70 percent was from the Asia Pacific region outside Singapore, while the city-state accounted for the remaining 30 percent.
During the year, Informatics opened 30 training centres, most of them in India, bringing the group's network of training centres to 140 in 21 countries.
Ong said he expected another 20 centres to be opened in the current year. He said focus will be on high growth areas like India, China, Indonesia and the Philippines.
